title: Scripted walks can press shifted letter shortcuts
goal: The automated walks the build loop uses to try the app can press a letter key, but not a capital one. That means any shortcut that needs Shift plus a letter (cycling the selection tools with Shift M, for example) cannot be checked automatically, so those shortcuts ship untested.
notes: Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PlaytestHarness.swift around line 491 builds the NSEvent with characters and charactersIgnoringModifiers both set to key.characters, the unshifted letter. AppKit key-equivalent matching for KeyboardShortcut("m", modifiers: .shift) wants "M" in charactersIgnoringModifiers, so the invisible stand-in button never fires. Fix: uppercase (or shift-map) characters when the shift modifier is present. Seen on 2026-09-02 while verifying the Current selection slot: step "key m + shift" logged "taken by window" but activeTool never became wand.
acceptance: A walk step that presses Shift plus a letter activates the shortcut bound to the capital letter
An existing shortcut that needs Shift plus a letter is proven working by a walk that fails if it regresses
